'''Tommy Ohlsson''' (born 13 June 1973) is a Swedish physicist. He is a full [[professor]] in [[theoretical physics]] with specialization in [[elementary particle physics]] at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] (KTH) in Stockholm, Sweden, situated at the [http://www.albanova.se/ AlbaNova University Center].<ref>Professor Tommy Ohlsson is working at the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, see http://www.kth.se/gemensamt/sok-anstalld?_flowId=user-flow&kthId=u1huti07&l=en_UK. Retrieved 2011-10-30.</ref> His research field is theoretical particle physics, particularly neutrino physics and physics beyond the so-called [[Standard Model]]. He is an author of around hundred scientific publications and one textbook (see Publications). He has also written a popular science text about the theory of special relativity at Nobelprize.org.<ref>"Relativity". Nobelprize.org, see http://www.nobelprize.org/educational/physics/relativity/ Retrieved 2011-12-02.</ref>

Ohlsson received his PhD at KTH in 2000 and was a postdoc at the [[Technical University of Munich]], Munich, Germany, between 2000 and 2002. He is employed at KTH since 2002 and was promoted to full professor in 2008. In 2003, he was awarded the Gustafsson Prize for young researchers at [[Uppsala University]] and KTH by the {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120525200348/http://www.gustafssonsstiftelse.se/uu_kth/index.html|title=Göran Gustafsson Foundation}}.<ref>The Göran Gustafsson Foundation - Prize Winners 2003 (in Swedish), see http://www.gustafssonsstiftelse.se/uu_kth/pris2003.html Retrieved 2011-10-30.</ref> Between 2005 and 2009, he held a research fellow position at the [http://www.kva.se/en/ Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (KVA)], which was funded by the [http://www.wallenberg.com/kaw/in_english/default.aspx Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation (KAW)].<ref>Tommy Ohlsson was a Research Fellow at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences between 2005 and 2009, see press release of appointment (in Swedish): http://www.kva.se/sv/pressrum/pressmeddelanden-2008-2001/Sju-unga-forskare-far-toppjobb-av-akademien/ Retrieved 2011-10-30.</ref>

In December 2012, Ohlsson was elected for a four-year term (2013–2016) to serve on [[arXiv]]'s member advisory board as one of eight voting members from the contributing organizations.<ref>Member Advisory Board, see https://confluence.cornell.edu/spaces/culpublic/pages/204734630/Member+Advisory+Board Retrieved 2013-02-03.</ref>

Since 1 January 2014 Ohlsson is the coordinating editor of the scientific journal [[Nuclear Physics (journal)|''Nuclear Physics B'']], which focuses on the domain of high-energy physics, [[quantum field theory]], statistical systems, and [[mathematical physics]].<ref>Nuclear Physics B - Journal - Elsevier, see http://www.journals.elsevier.com/nuclear-physics-b/ Retrieved 2014-08-26.</ref>
